title: Ham & Cheese Calzones
subtitle: golden homemade dough folded around ham, ricotta and melty mozzarella, with warm marinara for dipping
imageAlt: Two golden half-moon calzones, one cut open to show melted cheese and ham, with a small bowl of marinara, on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 4 calzones: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The dough needs 1 hour to rise; the rest is quick.
Drain any liquid off the ricotta so the calzones don't go soggy.

items.name: olive oil
items.note: 1 for the dough, 1 for the bowl and pan

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water and 1 tbsp of the oil, stir to a shaggy dough, then knead on the counter 5–6 minutes until smooth and springy.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Put it in a bowl rubbed with a little of the remaining oil, cover and let rise 1 hour, until doubled. After 40 minutes, heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Stir the ricotta, mozzarella, ham, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and pepper together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide the dough in 4 and roll each into a 20 cm round. Spoon a quarter of the filling onto one half of each, leaving 2 cm clear. Fold over, press the edges, then roll and crimp them tight.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set them on a baking sheet brushed with the last of the oil. Brush the tops with the egg and cut 2 small slits in each. Bake 18–20 minutes, until deep golden and the filling reads 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm the marinara while they rest 5 minutes, and serve it for dipping.

fixIt.fix: The edges weren't sealed or it was overfilled; crimp hard and keep the filling off the rim.
Bake on the lowest rack for the last 5 minutes.
Cover and rest it 10 minutes, then roll again.

saleTip: No Frills deli ham is cheapest in the pre-packed 175 g trays; mozzarella is often $4.99 on sale.
swap: Store-bought pizza dough: 900 g, divided in 4; let it sit out 30 minutes first.
leftovers: Wrap cooled calzones one by one; they make a great cold or reheated lunch.
doneness: Ham is fully cooked; bake until the filling reads 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, leftovers and reheated foods).
source: Based on tested homemade calzone methods (King Arthur Baking, Canadian Living): an instant-yeast dough risen 1 hour, filled with ricotta, mozzarella and ham, egg-washed and baked at 220°C.
prepAhead: Make the dough up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; bring it out 1 hour before shaping.
Mix the filling up to 2 days ahead.
reheat: At 180°C (350°F) for 12–15 minutes, or the air fryer at 170°C for 8 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Ham and mozzarella with ricotta; no Italian seasoning or egg wash.

stepNotes.4: Basic: brush with a little oil instead of egg.

fancy.note: Pepperoni inside and a garlic butter crust.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: lay a few pepperoni slices over the filling before folding.

addSteps.title: Garlic butter
addSteps.text: Brush the hot calzones with the butter mixed with the garlic powder and scatter the Parmesan over them.

plating: Cut one calzone open so the cheese stretches.
Marinara in a small bowl in the middle.

why.1-0: Ricotta keeps the filling soft and creamy instead of stringy.
why.2-0: Egg wash gives the shiny, deep golden crust.
why.1-2: Chopped ham spreads through every bite.

funFact: 'Calzone' means 'trouser leg' in Italian, from its folded, pocket-like shape.
airFryer: Air-fry 2 calzones at a time at 180°C (350°F) for 10–12 minutes, until deep golden and the filling reads 74°C (165°F).
